title: Markdown to print PDF/HTML exporter (fixtures)
context: Teachers need print-ready materials — a digital Markdown file is not walkable into a classroom. For lesson plans to be practically adoptable, they must export to print-ready PDF and/or HTML that a teacher can print or project. The Markdown canonical format (task-001) is the source of truth; PDF and HTML are build artifacts. This exporter must be deterministic (same input produces same output), fixture-tested in CI (so regressions are caught), and accessible (the output must be readable by screen readers and printable cleanly).
objective: Implement a deterministic Markdown-to-PDF and/or Markdown-to-HTML exporter for lesson plans, with committed golden-fixture tests verified in CI.
acceptanceCriteria: The exporter takes a lesson plan in Markdown + YAML front-matter and produces a print-ready PDF and/or accessible HTML output.
Output is accessible: semantic heading structure, alt-text for any images, and screen-reader-compatible markup in the HTML output.
The exporter is deterministic: the same input always produces the same output (or the same output modulo timestamps clearly documented).
Golden-fixture tests are committed: at least one canonical input plan and its expected PDF/HTML output are diffed in CI; a change to the exporter that alters output fails the fixture test.
The exporter uses an open-source toolchain (e.g. Pandoc, Puppeteer/Chrome headless, or a TypeScript PDF library) with pinned versions recorded.
Code is MIT-licensed; pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass; no credentials embedded.
resources: teacher-lesson-plans-template-001 — canonical lesson-plan schema and Markdown format
teacher-lesson-plans-validator-006 — existing schema validator (to integrate with)
PLAN.md — §Tech stack & key decisions (Markdown as source of truth)
output: A merged PR adding a Markdown-to-PDF/HTML exporter with golden-fixture tests integrated into the CI pipeline.
